source: Administration of Shipping & Ports — Meshit 30 Seamanship (boat operator) question pool, English edition, gov.il

topics: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
critical.label: rules of the road
critical.note: In the seamanship exam a wrong answer to a rules-of-the-road question — one whose consequence could be a collision or injury — fails the whole exam, even with a score above 90.

disclaimer: Text from the official English PDF; answers from the official answer key at its end. The key prints 253 twice and skips 252 — the answers follow the order of the rows, as in the Hebrew edition.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: When sailing a sailboat at night, you see in front of your bow the lights as depicted in picture 36, what is the required action?

options.a: You turn to starboard, and it must turn to starboard as well.
options.b: Maintain course and speed.
options.c: Yield because it is a large ship.
options.d: Make contact on the radio and inquire as to its intentions.

questions.question: What might a single white light in front of your bow be?

options.a: The stern light of a vessel.
options.b: A row boat.
options.c: The mooring light of a vessel under 50 meters long.
options.d: All the above answers are correct.

questions.question: What is the vessel depicted in picture 39?

options.a: A grounded vessel.
options.b: A limited maneuverability vessel due to draught, at anchor.
options.c: A ship not under command, at anchor.
options.d: A vessel in distress, requesting assistance.

questions.question: You have noticed the lights as depicted in picture 46. What is the vessel?

options.a: A pilot sailing to port.
options.b: A sailboat sailing to port.
options.c: A trawler sailing to port.
options.d: A sailboat sailing to starboard.

questions.question: What are the identifying signs for a marina entrance in Israel when coming in from sea?

options.a: A green light on the right and a red light on the left.
options.b: A red ensign (elongated triangular flag) flown on the right in addition to a blinking red light and a blinking green light on the left.
options.c: On the right a flashing green light and on the left a flashing red light.
options.d: On the right a flashing red light and on the left a flashing green light.

questions.question: What lights will a 100 meter long vessel with limited maneuverability vessel making its way display?

options.a: The lights as depicted in picture 66.
options.b: The lights as depicted in picture 2.
options.c: The lights as depicted in picture 25.
options.d: The lights as depicted in picture 22.

questions.question: What is the vessel displaying the lights as depicted picture 61?

options.a: A trawler.
options.b: The port side of a tug boat.
options.c: The starboard side of a mine sweeper.
options.d: The starboard side of a moored vessel over 50 meters long.

questions.question: What is the vessel displaying the lights as depicted in picture 28?

options.a: A fishing boat.
options.b: A trawler.
options.c: A towing vessel with the tow line less than 200 meters long.
options.d: A sailboat.

questions.question: What is the vessel displaying the lights as depicted in picture 8?

options.a: A fishing boat.
options.b: A tow boat with the tow line less than 200 meters long.
options.c: A trawler with a net over 150 meters long.
options.d: A tow boat pushing a barge.

questions.question: At the entrance to a marina in Israel there are two flashing lighthouses (red and green). What is their meaning?

options.a: At the entrance to a marina, the green lighthouse is on the starboard of the vessel and the red on its port.
options.b: At the exit from a marina, the green lighthouse is on the starboard of the vessel and the red on its port.
options.c: At the entrance to a marina, the green lighthouse is on the port of the vessel and the red on its starboard.
options.d: In any event you must pass to the starboard of the green and to port of the red.

questions.question: 50º to the starboard of your bow you notice a red light, underneath it a green light and underneath that a green navigation light. What is the vessel you are seeing?

options.a: A sailboat sailing to port.
options.b: A pilot.
options.c: A fishing vessel.
options.d: A sailboat sailing to starboard.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: A sailboat, sailing to north west, the wind from the north east, notices on its starboard flashing red + green lights (next to each other). What is the required action?

options.a: These are the lights of a sailboat windward on the same tack, she is up wind and will turn, you must maintain course and speed.
options.b: These are the lights of a sailboat on a port tack, she will turn, you must maintain course and speed.
options.c: It is the entrance to a marina, you increase watch and awareness, maintain course and speed.
options.d: There is no correct answer.

questions.question: While sailing, you notice in front of your boat’s bow a vessel displaying the lights as depicted in picture 39. What is the vessel signaling?

options.a: That it is grounded and so you must be careful.
options.b: That it is not under command and you must rapidly approach it and offer assistance.
options.c: That it is a fisherman collecting its nets. You may pass nearby.
options.d: It is a sailboat which has turned on its discretionary lights.

questions.question: A vessel displaying the lights as depicted in picture 39, what signal will it display during the day?

options.a: The signal depicted in picture 84.
options.b: The signal depicted in picture 81.
options.c: The signal depicted in picture 83.
options.d: There is no need for a day signal.

questions.question: What lights must you turn on when anchoring in a secluded bay with a vessel 13 meters long?

options.a: A sailboat will turn on a masthead light (steaming).
options.b: Surround white light.
options.c: Deck lights, stern light and masthead light (steaming).
options.d: A motorized vessel will turn on a top of mast light.

questions.question: You notice a vessel flying flag A: what does the flag mean, what are your actions and what will this boat display at night?

options.a: Diver flag, I will keep 200 meters away, at night a surround white light.
options.b: Diver flag, I will keep 200 meters away, at night a surround red white red light.
options.c: Diver flag, I will keep 200 meters away, at night a surround blue white light and navigation lights.
options.d: Diver flag, I will keep 200 meters away, at night there is a ban on diving.

questions.question: What is the vessel displaying the signs depicted in picture 78?

options.a: A barge being pushed by a tug boat.
options.b: A tug boat with a tow which is over 200 meters long.
options.c: A fishing vessel with the fishing equipment at work.
options.d: A tug boat, limited in maneuverability.

questions.question: What will a vessel display during the day that at night displays three red lights in a vertical line one above the other?

options.a: 3 black balls one above the other vertically.
options.b: 2 black balls.
options.c: A black cylinder.
options.d: A black diamond.

questions.question: At night you notice a vessel displaying, in addition to navigation lights, a white surround light and above it a green light. What is the day signal such a vessel should display?

options.a: 2 triangles with their bases joined.
options.b: 2 triangles with their tips joined.
options.c: A black diamond.
options.d: A circle diamond circle.

questions.question: A vessel displaying the lights depicted in picture 53, what day signal will it display?

options.a: The day signal depicted in picture 82.
options.b: The day signal depicted in picture 86.
options.c: The day signal depicted in picture 85.
options.d: There is no need for a day signal.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: You are in a sailboat at night, behind your stern you see the vessel lights depicted in picture 1, on an identical course to yours. With no additional information you know:

options.a: You are in danger of a collision because the direction to it is not changing.
options.b: That you will be in danger of a collision only if the distance decreases and the magnetic direction does not change.
options.c: That there is no danger of a collision in this situation.
options.d: That if he is behind you, in any case he has to give way, so there is no reason for concern.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: To what vessels must you give right of way when sailing a motorized vessel?

options.a: A vessel not under command.
options.b: A vessel with a capacity of 40 thousand tons and over.
options.c: A military vessel.
options.d: A towing vessel with a tow line of over 200 meters.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: How will a sailboat act when sailing in fog during the day, in limited visibility?

options.a: Turn on navigation lights, combined with the audible signal.
options.b: Turn on navigation lights only at sunset.
options.c: Only sound the audible signals.
options.d: May turn on the flashing yellow light in addition to the fog horn.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: You are sailing a 12 meter long vessel in the bay of Eilat at night under sails only. You are sailing slowly at a distance of about half a mile from shore. You turn on, as the law requires, side lights and stern lights. On your starboard appears a large tanker and you are directly in front of its bow. Mark the correct sentence:

options.a: The tanker must make way for me since I am a sailboat.
options.b: According to the rules of the open seas she must make way for me but in this case I am in its path and must make way to it.
options.c: I will turn on the discretionary lights (red over green), because these entitle me to right of way.
options.d: I get out of there because you are not allowed to stop in the bay of Eilat at night.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: To which of the following vessels must a motorized vessel en route make way?

options.a: A tug boat with no regard to the tow line length.
options.b: A tug boat, only if the tow line length from the stern of the tug to the stern of the tow is over 200 meters.
options.c: A vessel with limited maneuverability.
options.d: A passenger ferry.

questions.question: How will a motorized vessel act nearing the entrance to the Kishon port and from where it is located it is hard to determine that there are no vessels exiting the port?

options.a: Sail with special vigilance and caution and sound more than 5 short horn blasts.
options.b: Sail with vigilance and caution and sound one long horn blast.
options.c: The vessel must stop prior to entering, sound 3 short blasts, and if there is no vessel it can enter.
options.d: There is no special limitation at the entrance, only attention to the rocks at the entrance.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: A vessel “en route” means:

options.a: A vessel which is not making its way in the water but drifting.
options.b: A vessel tied to a dock.
options.c: A vessel making its way in the water under motor power.
options.d: A vessel not tied to a dock, not grounded, and not anchored.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: When will an overtaking and passing vessel yield way?

options.a: An overtaking and passing vessel will always yield.
options.b: When the passed vessel is lower than it on the “family hierarchy”.
options.c: Only when the passing is on the starboard side.
options.d: Only in limited visibility.

questions.question: You are sailing a sailboat in fog during the day, with the engine in forward gear. You are unable to see beyond 50 meters around your boat. How will you act?

options.a: I will turn on sailing lights only.
options.b: I will sound one long blast every two minutes.
options.c: I will sound 2 long blasts every two minutes.
options.d: I will turn on navigation lights and sound one long blast every two minutes.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: Your vessel is motorized with a working radar. You have discovered on the radar at night a vessel at 020 to your starboard at a range of 3 miles. With the naked eye it is difficult to see the navigation lights. After 10 minutes, the direction changes, to 018 starboard, range of 2 miles, and from the navigation lights it is still difficult to determine the precise sailing direction. What do you deduce from the information?

options.a: That the vessel is crossing from starboard to port and there is danger of a collision.
options.b: That the information is limited, and based on the regulations I must assume there is danger of collision.
options.c: That the vessel is sailing on an opposite course and parallel to mine and there is no danger of collision.
options.d: Answers “a” and “b” are correct.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: You are sailing close hauled on a port tack and in front of you is a sailboat on an indeterminate tack. How will you determine whether there is danger of a collision?

options.a: The compass direction does not change at all, and the distance remains constant.
options.b: There is no danger of a collision and I will not be able to pass it.
options.c: The compass direction does not change significantly and the distance is decreasing.
options.d: The compass direction changes significantly and the distance is decreasing.

questions.question: While sailing at night you notice a vessel which according to the rules of the road is supposed to yield to you but is not doing so. What are your initial actions?

options.a: I check if my navigation lights are on.
options.b: Sound 5 short blasts or more.
options.c: Turn aside quickly.
options.d: Answers “a” and “c” are correct.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: Who must yield when you are in a sailboat sailing with a broad reach on a starboard tack, on your starboard is a sailboat on a course almost parallel to yours which is bringing you slowly closer to danger of a collision. The other boat, “Sloop”, is sailing wing on wing, foresail to port and mainsail to starboard?

options.a: Your boat, because your maneuverability is better.
options.b: Your boat, because with a following wind it is possible to maneuver better than when running wing on wing.
options.c: The other boat because its mainsail is to starboard and this means a port tack.
options.d: Your boat because you are on the same tack and you are to windward.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: How will you act (based on the regulations) when you are sailing a sailboat on a port tack and on your port is another sailboat on a collision course and it is unclear what tack it is on?

options.a: Maintain course and speed.
options.b: You try to communicate with it to determine what tack it is on.
options.c: You yield.
options.d: You yield only if you can determine for certain that it is on a starboard tack.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: To which vessel must a sailboat en route yield?

options.a: A vessel with limited maneuverability.
options.b: A tug boat towing.
options.c: A tug boat, only if the tow line is over 150 meters long.
options.d: An on-duty police boat.

questions.topic: Rules of the road and collision avoidance
questions.question: How will a motorized vessel act, when noticing close on its bow a single green light?

options.a: Turn to starboard, the light indicates a sunken ship.
options.b: Continues straight, it is a race boat seeing me on its starboard and must make way for me.
options.c: Turn to port, this is the starboard light of a sailboat.
options.d: Stop, this is the light of a tow behind a tug boat.

questions.question: According to regulations, what areas are forbidden for sailing?

options.a: Bathing beaches, diving areas, closed areas.
options.b: Fishing areas, bathing beaches, anchoring areas.
options.c: Ports, bathing beaches, firing ranges.
options.d: Nature reserves, bathing beaches, security zones.

questions.question: What is meaning of “I.M.O.T.”?

options.a: Identification prior to entering the country, by a vessel to R.C.C. Haifa.
options.b: The international sailing safety organization.
options.c: The international maritime organization.
options.d: It is a chapter out of the S.O.L.A.S. book.

questions.question: To what distance away from shore may a vessel sail that is on a national voyage?

options.a: 6 miles.
options.b: No limitation.
options.c: 12 miles.
options.d: 35 miles.

questions.question: What are the boundaries of a bathing beach with no sailing allowed?

options.a: There are no uniform rules – each beach has its own boundaries.
options.b: 400 meters along the shore and up to 250 meters into the sea.
options.c: 50 meters on each side of the declared area and to a distance of 300 meters of the low tide line.
options.d: 100 meters on each side of the lifeguard hut, and 150 meters to sea from the high tide line.

questions.question: What additional item of equipment is required for a private vessel 13 meters long, sailing to a distance of 15 miles from shore?

options.a: G.P.S.
options.b: Additional pyrotechnic equipment.
options.c: Life raft.
options.d: V.H.F radio.

questions.question: When purchasing a boat you are interested in determining whether or not the importer equips the boat based on the requirements of the Israeli Seaworthiness Regulations. Where can you find this information?

options.a: The boat must be equipped according to the S.O.L.A.S. standard, which can be found in publications for sailors.
options.b: You can find the list of equipment in the Israel Ports Authority publications and on the Ministry of Transportation website.
options.c: You must submit a formal request to the technical department, as seamanship standards are different for each boat.
options.d: You can find the list of required equipment with Marina managers.

questions.question: What is required based on the regulations if there is open flame cooking on the boat?

options.a: A fire fighting blanket.
options.b: An automatic fire extinguishing system.
options.c: An additional CO2 fire extinguisher.
options.d: There are no additional requirements.

questions.question: When must a vessel turn on navigation lights?

options.a: 15 minutes before sunset until 15 minutes after sunrise.
options.b: 15 minutes after sunset until 15 minutes before sunrise.
options.c: Only when there is enough voltage in the boat batteries.
options.d: As in “a” and in addition whenever visibility is limited.

questions.question: What will you do with leftover food and garbage bags when you are over 3 miles from shore?

options.a: You can always throw garbage to the sea when you are over 3 miles from shore.
options.b: It is forbidden to throw garbage to sea at any time while sailing.
options.c: Only if the bag will sink.
options.d: It is forbidden if there is plastic in the bag.

questions.question: What is true of a life vest?

options.a: The number of life vests must equal the number of people on board as per the sea worthiness rating of the vessel.
options.b: Adult life vests also fit children.
options.c: Life vests of model 4 do not need to be ready for immediate use.
options.d: Life vests must be stored in a designated compartment for life vests.

questions.question: A vessel is displaying the sign depicted in picture 84 and sailing at about 100 meters from shore and parallel to it (where there is no declared swimming beach). What do the regulations stipulate about it?

options.a: It is breaking the law. It is a motorized sailboat.
options.b: It is allowed, it is a motorized vessel displaying a permit for sailing near the shore.
options.c: It is allowed, it is a fishing vessel at work.
options.d: It is breaking the law, it is a fishing vessel at work.

questions.question: What is the correct statement regarding the pyrotechnic equipment on board for an international voyage?

options.a: A smoke buoy operates for 6 minutes at least.
options.b: A parachute rocket goes up to a height of at least 3,000 meters.
options.c: A vessel must carry at least 4 parachute rockets.
options.d: A vessel must carry at least 4 hand torches.

questions.question: At what time intervals must a private boat be periodically inspected for sea worthiness?

options.a: Once a year.
options.b: Once every 24 months.
options.c: Once every 18 months.
options.d: Once every 30 months.

questions.question: What will you do when returning from an international trip with your boat, as you near Israel and are under 25 miles from shore?

options.a: Initiate communication on channel 16 with the Navy and report my location, identity, etc.
options.b: Initiate communication on channel 12 with the Haifa Port watch and report my location, identity, and anything else they request.
options.c: Initiate communication with RCC HAIFA on channel 16 (4X0) and report my location, identity, etc.
options.d: Initiate communication with the border checkpoint on channel 11 and report my location, identity, etc.

questions.question: What is the length of a sailing vessel defined as a boat?

options.a: 7 to 24 meters.
options.b: 20 to 70 feet.
options.c: 5 to 20 meters.
options.d: 7 to 24 feet.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate answer regarding the pyrotechnic equipment?

options.a: Pyrotechnic equipment is fit to be used up to 7 years.
options.b: A smoke buoy generates a flame that is very visible at night, especially to aircraft.
options.c: A red hand torch will continue to burn if it has fallen into the water.
options.d: A boat on a national journey must carry 4 smoke buoys.

questions.question: What is the correct statement regarding the pyrotechnic equipment on board for a national trip?

options.a: A parachute rocket goes up to a height of at least 3,000 meters.
options.b: A vessel must carry at least 4 parachute rockets.
options.c: A vessel must carry at least 4 hand torches.
options.d: A smoke buoy operates for at least 12 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following contains only distress signals?

options.a: A call for HELP on the VHF, a square flag plus a ball, the flags C + N.
options.b: The flags N + A, the sound of a cannon shot, a short horn blast.
options.c: A red rocket, a constant long horn blow, slow waving of the hands up and down on the side of the body.
options.d: Flames on the vessel, 3 black balls, transmitting SOS on the radio.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a distress signal?

options.a: Continuous gong rings.
options.b: A call of MAYDAY on the radio.
options.c: Raising of one flag from the international code.
options.d: Continuous horn blast with no stopping.

questions.question: Which of the following contains only distress signs or signals?

options.a: A black ball on the mast, C flag over N flag, waving of the arms on the sides of the body.
options.b: A square flag and above it a black ball, sounding of explosive sounds every minute, a non-ceasing horn blast, red rockets.
options.c: Activating the pyrotechnic equipment, transmitting S.O.S. on the radio, continuous bangs on the gong, more than 5 short horn blasts every 2 minutes.
options.d: A flag and above it a black ball, orange smoke, a man waving a red flag in his hand, display of a yellow hand torch.

questions.question: Which picture describes the audible signal that a sailboat will sound in fog?

options.a: Picture 112.
options.b: Picture 118.
options.c: Picture 120.
options.d: Picture 122.

questions.question: In fog you hear in front of your bow the audible signal described in picture 122, every 2 minutes, on the port of your bow you hear the audible signal described in picture 120 every 2 minutes. What is the meaning of the signals?

options.a: A ship stopped and not moving in the water.
options.b: A dredger busy digging.
options.c: A tug boat towing another vessel.
options.d: A motorized vessel towing a sailboat.

questions.question: You are sailing within a narrow sea lane and nearby are two ships sailing one behind the other. You, based on the regulations, are sailing so that you do not hinder the sailing of the ships. You hear the rear ship sounding the signal described in picture 116. What is the meaning of these horn blasts?

options.a: I change my course to starboard and his ship has stopped in the water.
options.b: I am about to pass you on your port.
options.c: I am about to pass you on your starboard.
options.d: Sailboat near me (meaning you), do not hinder my sailing.

questions.question: What is the vessel raising the flag described in picture 106 signaling?

options.a: Careful, do not come near, man overboard.
options.b: My ship is healthy, requesting permission for free operation within the port.
options.c: My boat is on medical quarantine.
options.d: A doctor is on board my boat.

questions.question: In poor visibility at night you hear the audible signal described in picture 118 every 2 minutes. What do the sounds mean?

options.a: Make way I am towing another vessel.
options.b: Be careful I am limited in maneuverability.
options.c: Requesting permission to pass you on the starboard side.
options.d: I am a motorized vessel not under way.

questions.question: Which picture describes the audible signal a motorized vessel would sound that is about to overtake another vessel on the port side?

options.a: Picture 116.
options.b: Picture 118.
options.c: Picture 120.
options.d: Picture 122.

questions.question: What is a vessel flying the flag described in picture 104 signaling?

options.a: Man overboard.
options.b: My boat is healthy, requesting permission for free operation within the port.
options.c: My boat is on medical quarantine.
options.d: A doctor is on board my boat.

questions.question: When entering a foreign port, you must fly the following flags:

options.a: On the port of the mast, an Israeli flag, and the flag of the host country to the starboard side of the mast.
options.b: In the stern, the flag of the host country, on the bow an Israeli flag (on a pole), to the starboard of the mast a Q flag.
options.c: On the starboard of the mast, the flag of the host country, to the port of the mast the Q flag, in the stern the Israeli flag on a pole.
options.d: To the starboard of the mast, the Q flag, and underneath it the flag of the host country, and to the port of the mast the Israeli flag.

questions.question: In front of you appears a vessel flying a white flag with blue split, how will you act?

options.a: I will maintain at least 200 meters distance from the vessel.
options.b: I will find out what the problem is (coordinate positions).
options.c: I will approach immediately, as immediate assistance is required.
options.d: There is no problem, it is the national flag of Monzia.

questions.question: Which of the following code flags must be on board a vessel?

options.a: A. B. C. Q. K. O
options.b: A. B. C. D. Q. O
options.c: N. A. B. C. Q. O
options.d: Z. O. Q. E. C. B.

questions.question: Which flags must you raise when entering the territorial waters of another country?

options.a: A yellow flag, the flag of the country of registration, the flag of the host country.
options.b: A green flag, flag of the country of origin, flag of the country of destination.
options.c: A blue flag, the flag of the most recently departed country, the flag of the host country.
options.d: A yellow flag, the flag of the shipping company, the national flag.

questions.question: What will your actions be when you are entering a marina and you recognize a vessel located near the entrance and flying flag “B” of the international code?

options.a: I cannot enter the marina since I must keep at least 200 meters from this vessel.
options.b: As in “a” but the safe distance for passage is only 100 meters.
options.c: I can enter the marina, but must be vigilant and avoid getting too close.
options.d: I will wait outside until the vessel clears way.

questions.question: In good visibility, a vessel to your starboard sounds at least 5 short horn blasts. What does the signal mean?

options.a: The vessel is turning to starboard.
options.b: The vessel is in distress.
options.c: Your actions are unclear.
options.d: There is no such signal.

questions.question: Which of the following vessels will sound, in limited visibility, a long horn blast followed by two short ones at two minute intervals?

options.a: A sailboat also running on motor.
options.b: A motorized vessel.
options.c: A fishing vessel.
options.d: Answers “a” and “c” are correct.

questions.question: You are sailing on vessel G and see vessel K sounding the audible signal described in picture 119. What is it signaling?

options.a: K is signaling that it is turning to starboard since it needs to yield way to me.
options.b: In fog this signal indicates that a vessel is not making way in the water.
options.c: That the vessel is in distress and needs help.
options.d: The signal is not clear so I will sound at least 5 short horn blasts because I do not understand his intentions.

questions.question: You are sailing on “F” and hear that vessel “H” sounds the following audible signal: three short horn blasts, 3 long horn blasts, 3 short blasts. What is the meaning of the horn blasts?

options.a: This is a vessel wanting to draw attention.
options.b: This is a vessel indicating that it is in distress.
options.c: There is no meaning to these horn blasts.
options.d: It is a vessel with its engines engaged in reverse because it has a man overboard.

questions.question: You are sailing a motor assisted sailboat. In front of your bow is a vessel flying a flag as depicted in picture 98. What lights must he display at night, and how should you act?

options.a: Lights as depicted in picture 26. It is indicating the side of a hazard, I can pass beside it with no concern.
options.b: Lights as depicted in picture 61. It is anchored and there is no danger in passing nearby.
options.c: Lights as depicted in picture 70. It is indicating a diving area and I must keep 200 meters distance from it.
options.d: Lights as depicted in picture 33. It is without control. I should approach as quickly as possible and offer assistance.

questions.question: Vessel F hears vessel H sounding the audible signal comprised of: six short blasts, three long blasts, six short blasts. What is the meaning of the horn blasts?

options.a: This is a vessel wanting to draw attention.
options.b: This is a vessel indicating that it is in distress.
options.c: There is no meaning to these horn blasts.
options.d: It is a vessel with its engines engaged in reverse because it has a man overboard.

questions.question: When will you use a parachute rocket?

options.a: Both during the day and at night.
options.b: At night only.
options.c: During the day only.
options.d: To light survivors.

questions.question: You must tow a 10 meter long yacht in open seas. The waves are 2 meters high. What tow rope will you prefer to use?

options.a: A 4 inch circumference rope, 10 meters long.
options.b: A 4 inch circumference rope, 50 meters long.
options.c: A 3 inch circumference rope, 20 meters long.
options.d: A 1*19 cable.

questions.question: What is a relative wind (virtual)?

options.a: The wind created only as a result of the boat movement.
options.b: The weighted value between the head wind and the real wind component.
options.c: The wind illusion created when the following wind is stronger than the vessel speed.
options.d: The wind the vessel operator estimates based on the sea waves.

questions.question: On a one engine and one shaft boat, with a right hand propeller, what will happen when you engage the engine in reverse?

options.a: The bow of the boat will veer to port.
options.b: The stern of the boat will veer to starboard.
options.c: The bow of the boat will veer to starboard.
options.d: There will be no veering and the steering will determine the direction.

questions.question: The emergency steering handle on a vessel with a steering wheel is there for situations where:

options.a: The steering cable breaks.
options.b: There is a break in the steering wheel axle.
options.c: The rudder breaks.
options.d: Answers “a” and “b” are correct.

questions.question: What must you avoid when sailing in a lightning storm with rain?

options.a: From nearing any metal objects on board.
options.b: From tightening the sail lines.
options.c: From touching water pipes.
options.d: From frequent course changes.

questions.question: The vessel is moving backwards. You want to turn the bow to starboard, in which direction must you turn the wheel (wheel steering)?

options.a: Starboard.
options.b: Port.
options.c: The wheel has no effect.
options.d: You must leave the steering wheel neutral, the deflection of the propeller will cause the turn.

questions.question: When there is a man overboard, you must toss a life ring with a light to the sea. How will the light be turned on?

options.a: You must turn it on before tossing it to sea.
options.b: The light will turn on when the life ring turns over and starts floating on the water.
options.c: The light is switched on by the person at sea once he reaches the life ring.
options.d: The light is switched on by a switch activated by contact with the water.

questions.question: What must you do when preparing to abandon ship and you have cast a life raft which inflated upside down?

options.a: You must immediately launch another life raft, because you cannot use a life raft which has been turned upside down, and it cannot be righted.
options.b: You must pull the rope tied to it, secure the raft to the side of the boat to windward, and then right it.
options.c: You send a swimmer who will stand on the gas container, grab the rope intended for it, and right the life raft.
options.d: Take the air out of the raft and inflate it again properly.

questions.question: What is the main function of the DROGUE (a type of floating anchor)?

options.a: Slow the vessel down when coming off high waves.
options.b: Prevent damage to the propeller when it leaves the water in waves.
options.c: Prevent the vessel rolling over in a storm.
options.d: Answers “a” and “b” are correct.

questions.question: You are sailing parallel to Herzliya close hauled, the wind you sense on your face is very strong, when you tack to running the wind you feel is much weaker. The reason for that is:

options.a: The wind velocity has suddenly dropped.
options.b: The speed is low, so the wind is weaker.
options.c: The relative wind (perceived) decreases and so you feel a weaker wind.
options.d: The head wind has weakened.

questions.question: You are sailing a motorboat and have run aground on a sandbank. What is the first action you will take?

options.a: Increase speed to pass the sandbank quickly.
options.b: Cast anchor immediately.
options.c: Abandon the boat immediately.
options.d: Put the engine into neutral.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the safety harness?

options.a: To secure equipment on the deck to avoid movement when rolling.
options.b: Tying the main sail boom in its place when the sail is down.
options.c: Safety of the crew in inclement weather to prevent going overboard.
options.d: Sealing the roller of the foresail, so it doesn’t open in strong winds.

questions.question: What is the most correct statement regarding the following situations when sailing under sails?

options.a: When close hauled: the lee way is large, the healing is strong, the speed is very high, the sail is in maximum stretch.
options.b: When running: the speed is high to medium, the healing is high, there is lee way, there is risk of capsizing.
options.c: In beam reach: the speed is high to very high, the lee way is small, there is healing.
options.d: In a close reach, the speed is lower than when close hauled, there is lee way, the sails are taught close to the keel line.

questions.question: You wish to anchor in a bay. What seamanship considerations will affect your decision?

options.a: Shore services, convenient dock, nearby restaurant.
options.b: The density of vessels moored in the bay, mooring services, availability of the responsible authorities.
options.c: The type of bottom, the wind direction and intensity, the density of vessels in the bay, the weather forecast.
options.d: There is no correct answer.

questions.question: What are the requirements of a tow rope?

options.a: High tensile strength.
options.b: Be of a natural material.
options.c: To be no longer than the length of the towing vessel so it does not get tangled in the propeller.
options.d: Answers “a” and “c” are correct.

questions.question: What will be your first actions when abandoning a vessel and after all the survivors are on board the life raft?

options.a: Activate the pyrotechnic equipment immediately to calm the survivors.
options.b: Have the survivors take a pill against sea sickness.
options.c: Distribute the food and water allotment for each survivor.
options.d: There is no correct answer.

questions.question: What of the following is the most effective way of determining that the anchor has secured to the bottom of the ocean and will not drag?

options.a: Taking bearings to other vessels.
options.b: Checking “vibrations” on the anchor line.
options.c: Checking your location by measuring the current.
options.d: By measuring the angle between the vessel and the perceived wind.

questions.question: What is the hydrostatic release of the life raft?

options.a: Serves as an additional security measure for the life raft.
options.b: Sounds an alarm in distress.
options.c: Releases the life raft automatically at a certain depth.
options.d: Releases the life raft when the crew is unable to release its security.

questions.question: What is a “dead anchor”?

options.a: An anchor permanently affixed to the sea bottom.
options.b: A floating anchor for emergencies.
options.c: A decommissioned anchor.
options.d: An anchor that has come loose and been lost.

questions.question: The administration of the marina where you are docked (sailboat), has instructed you to tie in parallel to another vessel (a sailboat identical to yours) due to congestion. How will you tie your boat?

options.a: You do not do side-to-side tying in a marina since this takes up a lot of space.
options.b: I will tie in parallel “bow to bow”.
options.c: I will tie in parallel “bow to stern”.
options.d: There is no significance as to how I tie the boat.

questions.question: What is your action immediately upon hitting a sandbar?

options.a: Raising two balls one above the other on the highest possible point.
options.b: If I have cast anchor, I must remove the two balls from point “a” and raise one ball only.
options.c: Empty the water and fuel, so the boat will rise and free itself from the sandbar.
options.d: Damage assessment and attempt to minimize damage based on the situation, prepare for abandoning or rescue.

questions.question: What are the topics on which you will brief and instruct passengers who are inexperienced, prior to a trip of several hours close to shore?

options.a: There is no need for any special explanation when going out for only a few hours.
options.b: I will explain the location and use of safety equipment.
options.c: I will explain how to navigate the boat based on the rules of the sea.
options.d: I will explain the importance of the skipper role on board.

questions.question: How is it recommended to reduce the load on the anchor winch, whenmooring?

options.a: You can use a rope that will tie to the winch chain and tie it to the bow deck cleat, and so divide the load between them and create an additional safety aspect.
options.b: You can secure the winch base and thus lower the load.
options.c: You can tie the anchor to the bow deck cleat intended for tying the chain.
options.d: You can move the anchor rope to the stern winch.

questions.question: What are the requirements of a mooring rope?

options.a: Fire proof.
options.b: To sink in the water.
options.c: High tensile strength.
options.d: All the above answers are correct.

questions.question: When entering the Herzliya marina, turning the steering wheel does not affect the boat’s maneuvering, what is your immediate option?

options.a: Engage the engine in reverse and increase RPM.
options.b: Attach the emergency steering handle on the axle of the rudder.
options.c: Cast anchor.
options.d: Transmit an urgent request for assistance.

questions.question: Which of the following ropes, of equal thickness, is the strongest?

options.a: Polypropylene.
options.b: Manila.
options.c: Nylon.
options.d: Kevlar.

questions.question: What is the “life rope” (safety)?

options.a: Life rope is a rope tied from bow to stern and used for attaching the safety harness while working on deck in stormy weather.
options.b: Life rope is a rope that is supposed to be installed on board at all times and secures the crew when climbing the mast.
options.c: Life rope is a rope attached to a life preserver and used for pulling people out of the water.
options.d: Life rope is a rope which enables saving lives in a stormy sea and used to slow the boat down in waves and prevent bow dive.

questions.question: Which is the correct sentence, in relation to tacking or gybing?

options.a: The diameter of the turn when gybing is smaller than when tacking.
options.b: The danger when tacking, is that the boom moves from side to side suddenly.
options.c: The danger when gybing is that the boom may move from side to side suddenly.
options.d: The danger when gybing is that the boat may come to a standstill with bow to the wind.

questions.question: What does a large heel of the boat cause?

options.a: Lowers the boat speed.
options.b: Improves steering.
options.c: Increases the boat speed.
options.d: Lowers the lee way.

questions.question: What is preferred for optimal mooring?

options.a: It is better to tie one rope tightly to a secure point, than two weak ropes which together will provide the same strength as the strong rope.
options.b: It is better to use two weaker ropes with one tied tightly and the other loosely.
options.c: It is better to tie as many ropes as possible, even if they are weak.
options.d: It is better to use two weak ropes for each tie point so that if one breaks the other will hold.

questions.question: You are sailing a 14 meter long boat with a 2 meter keel from Ashkelon to Haifa, at a distance of 2 miles from shore. Opposite the Tel Aviv harbor a south west wind of 25 knots has started, what will you do?

options.a: Return to Ashkelon.
options.b: Turn back and perform a HEAVE TO.
options.c: Continue north to shelter in the Herzliya marina.
options.d: Turn to the south east and enter the Tel Aviv marina.

questions.question: What is the effect of a knot or splice on a rope?

options.a: Any knot or splice on the rope weakens the original strength.
options.b: Any splice on the rope lowers its strength by one half of the original strength.
options.c: Any splice on the rope increases its strength by one quarter of the original strength.
options.d: Any knot on the rope increases its strength by one eighth of the original strength.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the marking 6/12 in cables?

options.a: 6 mains, 12 strings in each main.
options.b: 12 millimeter diameter, 6 ton work load.
options.c: 12 mains, 6 strings in each main.
options.d: 6 ton work load, 12 ton breaking load.

questions.question: What is the correct statement about a life raft?

options.a: The life raft inflates as the result of the impact from the fall to the water from a height of at least 2 meters.
options.b: Only the hydrostatic mechanism inflates the raft.
options.c: Under no circumstances should an inflatable raft be secured to the deck.
options.d: On the bottom of the raft is a strap for righting the raft.

questions.question: What is the primary use of a floating anchor?

options.a: To store objects that help anchoring for a vessel without an anchor.
options.b: To prevent drifting and maintain the bow or stern of the boat to the wind and waves.
options.c: Reduce the drift due to currents.
options.d: Answers “b” and “c” are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is forbidden while refueling the boat?

options.a: Verify that the fuel tank breather is free and aerated and there are rags for absorbing diesel fuel next to it.
options.b: Raise the B flag.
options.c: Leave the bilge pump switch on auto.
options.d: Have a crew member watch the fuel gauge.

questions.question: When sailing in a slow beam reach, on a starboard tack, you must turn into the wind. How will you act and what will you make sure of?

options.a: I must turn the boat to port.
options.b: The first step is to go downwind and release the main sail accordingly.
options.c: I will turn the wheel to starboard, if the ship stops facing the wind while turning one must reverse the direction of the rudder.
options.d: Nothing needs to be done, the difference in sail sizes and their lack of balance will turn the boat as needed.

questions.question: The boat is tied on its starboard side parallel to the dock with only one rope which serves as the stern brake, the engine is engaged in reverse and the steering wheel is centered. How will the boatreact?

options.a: The boat will move backwards along the dock.
options.b: The stern will veer to port.
options.c: The bow will veer to port.
options.d: The boat will not move at all, since the rope will not allow it.

questions.question: You are sailing parallel to the shore at a distance of about 500 meters from it. The wind increases and pushes the boat towards the shore, and you are five hours sailing away from your home anchorage. What action should you take?

options.a: I will return to the home anchorage.
options.b: I will move quickly away from the shore.
options.c: I will tow a floating anchor from the stern.
options.d: I will continue as planned.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the definition “TO RUN BEFORE”?

options.a: To sail against the wind and waves.
options.b: To sail with the wind and waves.
options.c: There is no such phrase in use for defining sailing with respect to the wind and waves.
options.d: During a sailboat race, an expression which means: “to precede the others”.

questions.question: The wind is east, you are on your way from Limassol (Cyprus) to Haifa on a course of 135°. At what approximate angle is the wind blowing on your boat? (angle and tack to the wind relative to the bow of the boat)

options.a: Starboard tack, about 045° from the bow.
options.b: Starboard tack, about 145° from the bow.
options.c: Port tack, about 045° from the bow.
options.d: Port tack, about 145° from the bow.

questions.question: How will you act initially when the anchor is dragging?

options.a: I will shorten the rope until the dragging stops.
options.b: I will release more anchor rope or chain.
options.c: I will move the tie point to the stern (less resistance).
options.d: All the answers are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is the most accurate regarding cables? (reading from left to right of the cable structure)

options.a: A 7x19 cable serves for securing the raft.
options.b: A 7x19 cable serves for the anchor as it is more flexible.
options.c: A 7x19 cable is the most rigid.
options.d: A 1x19 cable serves mostly for the safety railing.

questions.question: What is the TOPPING LIFT system used for on a sailboat?

options.a: To support and secure the boom when the mainsail is up.
options.b: To pull the boom downward in a strong wind.
options.c: As a raiser for the foresail.
options.d: To support and secure the boom when the main sail is lowered.

questions.question: You are sailing on a 090° course on a north wind, rated 4 on the Beaufort scale, (the boat has two masts). What will be the effect of carrying the following sails on your progress and on the steering? (the boat is balanced in terms of pressure)

options.a: When sailing on main sail only – the progress is quickest, the boat has a tendency to turn into the wind.
options.b: When sailing with a foresail only – the boat has a tendency to turn to a following wind.
options.c: When sailing with all sails – progress is quick and there are no steering issues.
options.d: Answers “b” and “c” are correct.

questions.question: The wind gauge shows 25 knots and the sea is white with foam. Describe and define the weather situation on the Beaufort scale.

options.a: Strong gusts, 7 on the Beaufort scale.
options.b: Strong wind, 3 on the Beaufort scale.
options.c: Very strong wind, 6 on the Beaufort scale.
options.d: Stormy weather, 5 on the Beaufort scale.

questions.question: Your boat Sloop is sailing in a headwind of 25 knots, with 4 meter waves, mainsail and foresail reefed. All of a sudden the foresail halyard breaks, you must send people to work on the bow, what is preferable (in terms of crew safety)?

options.a: Change to a beam reach and make sure the helmsman maintains course.
options.b: Continue on the present course and make sure the helmsman maintains it.
options.c: Change to running and make sure the helmsman maintains course.
options.d: Change to a broad reach wind and make sure the helmsman maintains course.

questions.question: What are your first actions when recognizing flooding on board?

options.a: Taste the water, activate pumps, seal openings.
options.b: Start the engine, transmit a distress signal, activate the pumps.
options.c: Transmit a distress signal on the radio, open a life raft.
options.d: Put on the life vests and head quickly to a marina.

questions.question: At what angle to the wind is the yacht in danger of an uncontrolled gybe?

options.a: When turning.
options.b: When running.
options.c: When in a broad reach.
options.d: When close hauled.

questions.question: Which of the following means help us determine that the sails are set correctly for sailing in a head wind?

options.a: Boat speed.
options.b: The lean of the yacht.
options.c: The limit of flutter of the foresail.
options.d: All the above answers are correct.

questions.question: How will the sails be set when the yacht is sailing close hauled?

options.a: The sails are loose.
options.b: The sails are tight to the keel line.
options.c: The foresail should be tight to the middle.
options.d: There is no need to set the sails.

questions.question: While sailing in the bay of Atlit you have hit a sandbar. What are your actions to get free from it?

options.a: I will empty the water and fuel so that the boat becomes lighter, I will ask the people to get off and into the water and I will try to get off the sandbar by engaging reverse gear.
options.b: I will engage neutral or lower sails, will conduct damage assessment and check the type of ground, and then call the insurance company emergency center to get further instructions.
options.c: I will engage neutral or lower the sails and conduct damage assessment, and if possible I will try to free the boat by engaging reverse.
options.d: I can free the boat by increasing speed and engine RPM and trying to skip over the sandbar.

questions.question: You are sailing a sailboat in direction 300º, the wind is north at 10 knots. You would like to change the sailing course to 060º. What is the most effective action you can take?

options.a: I will turn the steering wheel to starboard and perform a gybe.
options.b: I will turn the steering wheel to starboard and perform a tack.
options.c: I will turn the steering wheel to port and perform a gybe.
options.d: I will turn the steering wheel to port and perform a tack.

questions.question: You are sailing a sailboat in direction 120º , the wind is west at 30 knots, and you would like to change direction to 060º . What is the most effective and safest action you can take?

options.a: I will turn the steering wheel to starboard and perform a gybe.
options.b: I will turn the steering wheel to starboard and perform a turn.
options.c: I will turn the steering wheel to port and perform a gybe.
options.d: I will turn the steering wheel to port and perform a turn.

questions.question: You are sailing a 12 meter long boat heading north west (on board in addition to yourself are 5 crew members for whom this is a first sailing. 3 of them are children). The wind is south west (240º) at 15 knots with gusts to 20 knots. You are sailing with full sails and your boat assumes a strong healing every time there is a wind gust. You would like to change the situation. What should you do?

options.a: I will turn upwind to a close haul and reduce the healing.
options.b: I will flutter the sails during wind gusts.
options.c: I will go downwind to running in order to reduce the healing.
options.d: I will reef the sails and consider sailing on foresail alone.

questions.question: What are the most important things you will brief inexperienced people on prior to a sailing of several days?

options.a: There is no need for a detailed briefing prior to departure, we have a whole week to learn to operate the boat. I will explain to them about the assistance I will need during engine maneuvers.
options.b: I will explain about the dangers of going overboard, the assistance I will need during the sailing, ask them to alert me to anything they think is out of the ordinary, advise them to be careful with fire, the actions when abandoning ship and the workings of the toilet.
options.c: I will explain the principles of engine maneuvers and basic rules of the sea, actions when abandoning ship and the location of the life raft.
options.d: I will explain to them about what we should expect in the coming week, about the course for the first day, the meaning of life on a boat, the conservation of water, the working of the toilet, conserving electricity, the rules of environmental friendliness and the assistance I will need.

questions.question: How should ropes be maintained?

options.a: They should be replaced periodically.
options.b: Wash them in sweet water and dry and store them in the shade.
options.c: Roll them up following use, and keep in a locker.
options.d: Most of the ropes are synthetic and do not require special maintenance.

questions.question: What are the desired characteristics of an anchor rope and what rope would you prefer to use?

options.a: A sinking rope, and non-stretching.
options.b: A stretchable rope, floating, braided rope.
options.c: A stretchable rope, floating, interwoven.
options.d: A stretchable and sinking (non-floating) rope.

questions.question: You would like to make a turn in a narrow channel, the width of the channel is slightly greater than the length of your boat. You boat has a right hand propeller, through which side would you prefer to turn (assuming the wind is negligible)?

options.a: I would prefer to turn through the starboard side so I can use the prop work when moving backwards.
options.b: I would prefer to turn through the starboard side so I can use the offset.
options.c: The wind is more significant than the prop work so there is no importance to the side through which I choose to turn.
options.d: I would prefer to turn through the stern since the axis of turn moves backwards.

questions.question: You have tied a 19 meter boat to a refueling dock at a marina, the wind is pushing you into to the dock and you would like to depart from there. What is a possible solution to this challenge?

options.a: I will issue instruction to move the bow out with a pole and I will exit bow forward.
options.b: I will move the stern away from the dock and exit with the bow forward.
options.c: I will use a bow brake (spring) and fender in the bow and engage engine forward.
options.d: I will use a bow brake (spring) and fender in the bow and sail by engaging engine to reverse.

questions.question: You are interested in Mediterranean mooring in one of the marinas in Greece. Where can you find information on the marina and mooring location?

options.a: In the pilot book, sea charts and information from friends who have sailed in the area.
options.b: In the pilot book, tour guides, and almanac.
options.c: There is no structured literature for the Greek Islands in Hebrew, I must approach slowly and check every single location.
options.d: In the almanac and in the anchorages and ports guide.

questions.question: When will you prefer to dock with the bow to the dock as opposed to the stern to the dock?

options.a: When there is a strong wind and I have a hard time sailing backwards.
options.b: When the depth changes near the dock and there is fear of hitting the rudder.
options.c: When I am interested in privacy.
options.d: Answers “b” and “c” are correct.

questions.question: You are tied to a dead anchor using a mooring line. What is the danger when leaving?

options.a: That when releasing the rope I will fall on the boat next to me.
options.b: That there is no possibility of using the rope as assistance in maneuvering.
options.c: That it is not possible to engage the engine until the rope has sunk.
options.d: There is no correct answer.

questions.question: How can you determine if your boat’s anchor is dragging?

options.a: There is no way to know if the anchor is dragging you must keep anchor watch as long as the boat is anchored.
options.b: The bow of the boat will remain into the wind but the boat will move backwards.
options.c: There will be no vibrations on the anchor chain and I will feel the boat changing location.
options.d: There will be vibrations on the anchor line and the boat will not maintain its bow to the wind.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of actions when mooring?

options.a: Select the mooring location, brief the crew, reach the mooring location with the wind on the stern, stop, cast anchor and use reverse gear to plant the anchor.
options.b: Select the mooring location, brief the crew, reach the mooring location bow to the wind, stop, cast anchor and check if the anchor is dragging.
options.c: Select a mooring location, set the anchor line length and prepare it on board, approach the mooring location and cast the anchor while moving backwards.
options.d: While moving forward cast the anchor, stop the boat and check if the anchor is dragging.

questions.question: What are your actions when a man goes overboard in a stormy sea while sailing on sails?

options.a: Call the person in the water, toss a life preserver, maintain visual contact, turn to a beam reach and perform a man at sea maneuver.
options.b: Call the person in the water, toss a life preserver, press MOB on the navigation system, maintain visual contact, turn to a beam reach and perform a man at sea maneuver.
options.c: Toss a life preserver, roll in the foresail, start the engine and approach the person in the water.
options.d: Call the person in the water, toss a life preserver with a rope, perform a heave to and wait for the person to swim to you.

questions.question: You are sailing to Cyprus and suddenly hear a call for help and towing from an Israeli sailboat which is 90 miles from Cyprus. The weather is good but the forecast predicts a low pressure in 48 hours (the request for towing is due to engine failure). What will your actions be?

options.a: Lower sails and immediately proceed to rescue the boat, based on the rules of the sea I must assist a vessel in distress.
options.b: Lower sails, prepare a towing triangle in the stern, approach the boat from the windward side and tow it carefully to Cyprus.
options.c: Check if I am able to perform the tow (fuel status, appropriate ropes, etc.), I have no obligation to assist the boat since it is not in distress.
options.d: I will proceed to it from windward and tow it to Haifa since Haifa is closer.

questions.question: A 10 knot wind is blowing directly from the south, you are sailing on sails on a course of 205°, the steering is limp in your hands and you have trouble maintaining course. What is the reason for that?

options.a: The wind is probably too strong.
options.b: You are too “close” to the wind, and your speed in the water is too low.
options.c: The wind must be too weak.
options.d: You are too “close” to the wind, and your speed in the water is too high.

questions.question: In the CARDINAL buoy system you see a yellow and black buoy, and above it this symbol . From where should you pass the buoy?

options.a: You must pass the buoy to the north.
options.b: You must pass the buoy to the south.
options.c: You must pass the buoy to the east.
options.d: You must pass the buoy to the west.

questions.question: How will lowering one of the sails affect a two mast boat reaching in a beam reach? (the boat is trimmed in terms of pressure)

options.a: Lowering the mainsail will cause the boat to turn windward.
options.b: Lowering the foresail will cause the boat to turn windward.
options.c: Lowering the aft sail will cause the boat to turn windward.
options.d: Lowering the mainsail will cause the boat to turn leeward.

questions.question: Which factors must you take into account when towing another vessel?

options.a: The sea condition, the fuel quantity, the strength of the tie point.
options.b: The fuel quantity, the number of crew on the towed vessel and if it is according to the ministry of transportation regulations.
options.c: If the towed vessel is larger and heavier than the towing vessel, this is impossible from a physics point of view.
options.d: All the above answers are correct.

questions.question: What is the reason that when a boat is turning, it is recommended to turn the rudder to a maximum angle of 45° to the keel and no more?

options.a: This angle represents a 90° counter to the forces at work and the resultant force is the shortest vector.
options.b: At an angle greater than 45° the turning force is greater than the braking force.
options.c: At 45° the turning force to braking force ration is optimal.
options.d: At 45° the braking force is minimal.

questions.question: The weight of your rubber boat with an outboard motor is 320 kilograms. You attach to the end of the main boom a set of pulleys so that 4 cables extend from the moving pulley (the one which attaches to the rubber boat) and you would like to lift the boat using the pulleys. Ignoring friction, what is the force required to lift the boat?

options.a: 64 kilograms.
